claimed_purpose.text: A hierarchical tree-structured long-term memory system shared between the AI and user, framed as an extension of the model's brain rather than an external database.
Nocturne Memory uses a boot protocol triggered at session start to load persistent memory via a dedicated resource URI.
All AI modifications across namespaces are treated as a unified set of changes to avoid complex rollback races.
Certain memory URIs are auto-loaded on boot to define the AI's core identity on every startup.
Nocturne Memory organizes memories into named domains as top-level namespaces.
Multi-agent and multi-persona isolation use case

mechanisms.text: Write path for update (content): inserts a new Memory row on the same node_uuid, then deprecates old active memories by setting deprecated=True and migrated_to=new_memory_id; new row is then set deprecated=False
Persisted store has four tables: Node (conceptual entity, UUID), Memory (versioned content row), Edge (parent→child with metadata), Path (materialized URI cache mapping domain://path to an edge)
The system uses a graph service with create, update, alias, delete, and version chain operations, suggesting graph-based memory storage with versioning and conflict/supersession support.
The boot-time memory read can be triggered invalidly (a spurious `read_mcp_resource` call fires on startup), indicating the retrieve step is not precisely bound to the intended protocol.
Content–path separation: memory content is stored once under a unique Memory ID; multiple URI aliases can point to the same content with independent disclosure conditions and priority.
Disclosure field on each memory node is a trigger condition that instructs the agent when to call read_memory; it is a scaffold instruction, not an automatic retrieval mechanism
The project distinguishes between a memory system that mimics human memory and one optimised for agentic tasks, suggesting two distinct design philosophies for persistence.
Human audit layer: every AI write generates a snapshot reviewable via Dashboard; cleanup (purging old versions and orphaned memories) requires explicit human confirmation
Glossary triggers bind keyword terms to memory nodes; when a trigger word appears in any memory's content, read_memory surfaces a glossary link to the bound node
Isolation is per namespace: Path rows carry a namespace field; all queries filter by namespace; cross-namespace nodes are hidden from callers
The deployment uses a backend API container named nocturne_memory-backend-api-1, with a snapshots directory as part of the persistence path
Write path includes add, modify, and delete; changes produce a before/after diff visible in the web dashboard, user accepts or rolls back
Memory is stored in a self-hosted MCP Server, separate from chat platforms; MCP-compatible clients connect to the same long-term state
Uses structured hyperlinking with Aho-Corasick keyword matching instead of vector embeddings to connect related memories automatically
Memories are organized into named domain namespaces (e.g. core, writer, game, notes); 'system' is always available internally.
Named tables that are tracked in the changeset store include 'memories', 'nodes', 'edges', 'paths', and 'glossary_keywords'.
Cross-model read of the same long-term memory is supported, but persona expression may differ due to differing base models
Random retrieval is weighted by staleness × priority multiplier so older and higher-priority memories surface more often
A fixed set of memory URIs is loaded at every boot to scaffold the AI's identity before any conversation begins.
Memories are stored in either SQLite or PostgreSQL, selectable via DATABASE_URL; both backends are supported.
A public read-only mode exists that restricts write tools; the feature was introduced in commit 6a482ba.
Retrieve index covers path, content, disclosure, and glossary keywords as fields in the search document
Backend uses a database with an absolute-path DATABASE_URL, suggesting a local persistent store
Persistence backend supports SQLite or PostgreSQL; can run locally or self-hosted on a server
Memory is stored in a SQLite database; the data file path is user-configured.
Delete severs the access path only; it does not delete memory content itself
Review and rollback enhancement flagged as high-risk core model change
Persistence is cross-model and cross-session by design

ledger.claim: Persistent store is SQLite (local) or PostgreSQL (remote/multi-device); memories survive across sessions and model switches
ledger.quote: Nocturne Memory adopts a minimalist but highly available SQLite/PostgreSQL + URI Routing architecture. Completely open-source, it targets local single-agent execution with SQLite, and seamlessly scales to remote multi-device state synchronization via PostgreSQL.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Boot URIs scaffold: designated memories load automatically at every session start via system://boot, providing identity continuity without loading the full store
ledger.quote: On startup, system://boot automatically loads these core memories. The AI wakes up knowing who it is, who its user is, and what its mission is. Configure once, awaken forever.
ledger.locator: Section: 🔥 This Is Not Another RAG Memory System, solution table row ❺
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conditional recall via per-memory disclosure field; recall is triggered by context match against the disclosure condition, not by cosine similarity
ledger.quote: Each memory is bound to a human-readable trigger condition (disclosure), e.g., 'When the user mentions project X.' AI injects contextually, not blindly.
ledger.locator: Section: 🔥 This Is Not Another RAG Memory System, solution table row ❸
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Delete operation severs path, not content; content is versioned and recoverable
ledger.quote: delete_memory: Sever an access path (does not delete the memory content itself)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Version chain on Memory entity uses deprecated + migrated_to fields; rollback to any prior version is supported
ledger.quote: `deprecated` + `migrated_to` version chain enables one-click rollback to any historical version

ledger.claim: Cross-node hyperlinks are auto-generated at write time via Aho-Corasick keyword matching when trigger words appear in memory content
ledger.quote: Bind keywords to memory nodes (e.g., 'Salem' → core://my_user). When any memory's content contains that keyword, the system detects it via Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching and auto-generates cross-node hyperlinks.
ledger.locator: Section: 🔥 This Is Not Another RAG Memory System, solution table row ❹
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Human confirmation required before purging deprecated versions or orphaned memories; the AI cannot self-delete its own version history without owner approval

ledger.quote:
Node: a conceptual entity (UUID), version-independent
- Memory: a content version of a node
- Edge: parent→child relationship between nodes, carrying metadata
- Path: materialized URI cache (domain://path → edge)

ledger.claim: Soft forget marks memories deprecated=True and keeps them recoverable; hard delete is a separate explicit human action

ledger.claim: Isolation is enforced at query time by namespace filter on Path rows; cross-namespace nodes are hidden
ledger.quote:
If this edge has no Path in the current namespace, the child
node belongs to a different namespace. Skip it rather than
falling back to edge.name, which would expose cross-namespace
nodes to the caller.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval is by explicit path lookup or weighted-random surfacing; no adaptive/semantic retrieve policy is implemented in this file
ledger.quote:
Pick a weighted-random memory node. Weight = staleness * priority_multiplier.
Older and higher-priority memories are more likely to surface.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Cycle prevention: adding an edge that would make a descendant an ancestor is refused
ledger.quote:
Check if adding edge parent_uuid->child_uuid would create a cycle.

Returns True if child_uuid can already reach parent_uuid by
following existing edges downward

ledger.claim: Orphaned memory and node rows created in the same changeset as a net-zero path are garbage-collected from the pool.
ledger.quote: Related node/memory/edge entries created in the same changeset (before=None) lose their path mapping and become invisible to the review UI while still being counted as pending changes. This sweeps them out.
